beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:wonder, setting the scene][tune:level]Along the east coast of the United States lie half a ^million oval hollows... [act:the eerie detail, slower][tune:fall]all pointing the ^*same* way.
[d:tension][act:posing the big question, intrigued][tune:rise]^Craters, from ^one blast in the sky?

[d:calm][act:plain storytelling, a guided tour]They're called the Carolina ^Bays, and they dot the flat coastal plain from New Jersey to ^Florida. [go:1|0][p:0.93][act:giving a sense of scale]The smallest cover less than a hectare: about one football ^pitch. [act:giving a sense of scale]The biggest cover thousands of acres: several square ^kilometres. [act:observing closely][tune:fall]Most are shallow, with a sand ^rim on their ^south-east end.
[d:build][go:2|0][sfx:shimmer][act:intrigued, building the mystery]And their long axes@axis swing ^smoothly as you travel north, as if they all fanned out from ^one point.

[d:build][act:laying out the claim, fair and vivid]So the idea: about twelve thousand eight hundred years ago, a ^comet hit the great ice sheet to the north. [act:vivid, the claim at its strongest]Chunks of ice rained down across the east, and punched half a million craters at ^once.

[d:aside][act:playful, childlike curiosity][tune:fall]Now, the question a ^six-year-old asks first: where are the ^rocks that hit? [d:build][act:matter of fact, turning a page]Then came the ^dating. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an everyday picture]Grains of sand work like tiny ^batteries: sunlight empties them, and once buried, they slowly ^recharge. [act:explaining, clear]Measure the charge, and you know how long the sand has lain in the ^dark. [act:slow, spanning the ages][tune:level]Rim sands from a ^hundred and nine thousand years ago... [act:landing it, clear][tune:fall]to ^two thousand. [act:quiet, deliberate][tune:fall]^Built and ^rebuilt, over ages.

[d:list][go:5|0][act:calm, precise]Beneath them, the older layers lie flat and ^undisturbed. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]A real blast would leave crushed grains and melted ^rock. [act:flat, pointed][tune:level]No ^shock. [act:same flat weight][tune:fall]No ^melt.

[d:reveal][act:leaning in, the decisive detail]Then there's White ^Pond, one of the bays, where impact ^markers were reported. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an everyday picture]Mud settles on a pond floor year after year, like dust on a ^shelf: the deeper, the ^older. [sfx:hit][act:the decisive detail]Even there, the lake mud goes back ^thirty-one thousand years. [act:quiet, certain][tune:fall]The bay was there ^long before.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:calm authority, the slow answer]^Wind@air and waves on old ponds, over ^tens of thousands of years, slowly stretching and smoothing their ^shores. [act:the other option, even][tune:rise]^One blast? [act:the verdict, firm][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out* by the dates.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:fair, generous][tune:fall]The ^pattern is real. [act:a knowing smile, unhurried][tune:level]The ^cause is just... [act:the last word, gentle][tune:fall]^*slower*.
